pages.lesson:
LESSON: PAIRED READING

Grade: Grade 2
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES
Strand: READING
Topic 3.1: Paired reading

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Paired reading. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. provide feedback on peer’s reading
2. ask questions to confirm and extend understanding of material read
3. make predictions before and during reading e) appreciate the importance of turn- taking and listening to peers as they read 160

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. provide feedback on peer’s reading
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to provide feedback on peer’s reading. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. ask questions to confirm and extend understanding of material read
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to ask questions to confirm and extend understanding of material read. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

3. make predictions before and during reading e) appreciate the importance of turn- taking and listening to peers as they read 160
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to make predictions before and during reading e) appreciate the importance of turn- taking and listening to peers as they read 160. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: When you meet your teacher in the morning, say “Good morning” clearly and smile.

Example 2: Listen to a short story about a child walking to school. Then tell a friend one thing that happened.

Example 3: Write three sentences about your school using new words from this lesson.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Paired reading.
2. Explain Paired reading to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Paired reading.
4. Show that you can: provide feedback on peer’s reading
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Paired reading. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why is Paired reading important to you?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. provide feedback on peer’s reading
2. ask questions to confirm and extend understanding of material read
3. make predictions before and during reading e) appreciate the importance of turn- taking and listening to peers as they read 160

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Learner lesson
